symptom: `describe microflow ModA.MF_A; describe microflow ModA.MF_B` of two mutually recursive microflows, re-checked against a project without them, failed: "microflow ModA.MF_A references microflow ModA.MF_B before it is created (statement 3), and the project does not have it"; plain creates got MDL-ORDER01. No order of the two statements passes, so mutual recursion could not round-trip without a hand-written stub (mendixlabs/mxcli#1405).
cause: The flow builder resolved a CALL MICROFLOW/NANOFLOW target in statement order (microflowExists against the project; ctx.scriptFlows was filled only by check's verdict pass, with earlier statements), and MDL-ORDER01 / validateForwardDefRefs mirrored that refusal (#955). But a call is stored by name (MicroflowCall.Microflow, QN parameter mappings), so the BSON is the same whether the callee exists yet; the only hazard was a later statement failing and leaving the call dangling, which #1408's all-or-nothing journal removes.
file: mdl/executor/executor.go (SetForwardFlowCalls, enterScriptFlows fills scriptFlows from the whole program); mdl/executor/validate_definition_order.go (defRef.flowCall: skipped by MDL-ORDER01, refused by validateForwardDefRefs only when the run cannot roll back); mdl/executor/validate.go (annotateForwardRef hint); cmd/mxcli/cmd_exec.go, cmd_check.go, cmd_diff.go (mode)
insight: The rule was right for the mode it was measured in, not for the language: a forward reference is unsafe only where a later failure cannot be undone. So the exemption is per run mode (plain exec and check accept; --continue-on-error, REPL, -c refuse with the stub recipe) and per reference kind — only flow-call targets, because a page button's flow and an IN QUEUE target are still resolved eagerly when written (TestForwardFlowCall_PageReferenceStillOrdered pins one). Measured on Mendix 11.6.6: A<->B microflows and nanoflows in either order, exec then mx check 0 errors, describe -> exec -> describe identical.
